n1.text: The baker at {bakery} slides a warm, lumpy-looking loaf towards you. "New recipe," she says. "I need honest tasters, and I need a name." It smells of honey and toasted seeds.

choices.label: Ask who else could taste it

n2.text: You take a slice. Honey first, then a nutty crunch, then a surprising little hint of pepper. The baker waits with her pencil raised. "Honest, please. I can take it."

choices.label: Say it needs a pinch more salt
Say it's lovely as it is

n3.text: "Good thinking," says the baker. "More opinions, more bread." She wraps two thick slices in paper and tucks them into your hands. "Take them wherever you like."

n4.text: The baker nods and writes it down. "Salt. Of course." She bakes a small second loaf, and it is even better: rounder, deeper, just right. "Now it only needs a name."

n5.text: The baker laughs. "Kind of you. But honest tasters find one small thing, and so do I. Be brave." You chew a little longer, and she is right. Something is missing.

choices.label: Own up: it needs more salt

n6.text: Queen Rose pours tea and tries the bread in {queenParlour}. "Mmm. Wonderful with butter. And a little jam, I think." She dabs her fingers on a napkin. "Tell the baker it is a loaf for sitting down with."

choices.label: Carry her advice to the baker

n7.text: In {jokerCaravan}, Robin pulls a slice from behind your ear, takes a bite, and bows. "Riddle me this: what is round, speckled, and gone by noon?" Robin grins and waits.

choices.label: Take the riddle back to the baker

n8.text: The baker chalks "Honey Hearth" on the board by the door of {bakery}. By the afternoon, the first customers are asking for it by name. She saves you the warm end slice, and you eat it happily.

n9.text: Back at {bakery}, the baker reads the name aloud and smiles. "Good Morning Loaf. Simple, and it makes you want some." She writes it on the board and hands you a slice for the road.

n10.text: You pass on the Queen's advice at {bakery}. The baker sets out butter and jam beside the loaf and calls it the Parlour Loaf. "Fit for a Queen," she says, and you agree, with your mouth full.

n11.text: "Right!" cries Robin, delighted, and follows you to {bakery}. The baker chalks "Gone by Noon" on the board. By twelve, there is only one crumb left, and Robin makes it vanish with a flourish.
